summary.name: Yardlet
summary.one_liner: Yardlet is a free, open-source native Mac app, written in Swift, that runs coding agent CLIs such as Codex and Claude Code side by side in one window, using each agent's own sign-in and sessions.
keywords: codex claude code side by side
opencode cursor agent antigravity kimi grok
use_cases: Running Codex and Claude Code side by side on one Mac
Having one agent review another agent's changes
Reviewing diffs and merging pull requests from agent work
Scheduling agent tasks while the app is open
Approving agent actions from an Android phone
Letting agents use Gmail, Google Calendar or Google Drive via connectors
summary.what_it_does: Yardlet starts agent CLIs (listed as Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor Agent, Antigravity CLI, Kimi Code, Grok Build, Hermes Agent, Muse Code and Pi) with the sign-in they already have and gives them a shared sidebar, conversation view, composer and approval cards. Agents can read, message, and start tasks on each other, run subagents on other agents, and wait for results, with approvals required for cross-project actions. It shows diffs, a terminal, files, and a pull request card that follows checks through the user's gh CLI. It includes an embedded Chromium browser that agents can drive, with a password vault that fills sign-ins only on the matching site, and connectors for Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, GitHub, Slack and remote MCP services. Sessions stay in each agent's own store, and Yardlet writes nothing into agent configuration.
notable: Native Swift Mac app, not a web view, that reuses each agent's own CLI sign-in and session history
Agents can hand work to each other, with approval cards and the user's own words passed along
Per-account session and weekly limit display; new tasks go to the account with the most room left
No analytics; the only online services are an update check and an optional phone relay that is end-to-end encrypted
caveats: Requires macOS 15 or later and Apple silicon; Homebrew install is the other route
Android companion app is not public yet
Google sign-in shows an 'unverified app' warning until Google finishes reviewing Yardlet, unless you use your own OAuth app
User must install and sign in to at least one agent CLI first
